subject: Zenith-Orbit model intake: urgent pin & compatibility scan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Zenith-Orbit model intake: urgent pin & compatibility scan

Team —

NeuroScale just sent over Zenith-Orbit v1.2 for integration (contact below). They flagged a nonstandard KV-cache layout and a custom tokenizer migration path that broke our quantized eval in a quick smoke run yesterday. Im asking for a short-term version pin while we complete a compatibility scan because this model is included in an upcoming partner demo next week and we can't risk a mishit if runtime selects an incompatible variant.

Ask: can infra + runtime reserve a pin for v1.2 for the next 48 hours (canary) while we run the compatibility suite? If the canary looks green, well propose a staged rollout. If not, we need an automatic fallback to v1.1 for the partner route.

What I'm attaching: Zenith-Orbit manifest (zenith-orbit_v1.2-manifest.json) and the Manifest->KV mapping excerpt. External contact is Kevin O'Neil (kevin@neuroscale.ai) — he can provide the full tokenizer migration notes and a signed MAP if needed.

Questions I have for you:
- Lauren: how long to complete a full tokenizer/kv compatibility pass on our standard harness?
- Karthik: can we pin a variant for 48h on a dedicated canary pool (A100) without disrupting other pools? Any telemetry tags we should apply?
- Dylan: will this need additional QA/edge-case prompts from product to validate behavior? I'll assemble a quick evaluation prompt set if so.

Timelines: NeuroScale wants this validated by EOD Aug 11 to keep the demo on schedule. If you need procurement/legal involved for pinning beyond 72 hours, flag that early and I'll loop them in.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Model Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: zenith-orbit_v1.2-manifest.json (attachment stub)

Marcus — quick notes from infra/engineering perspective:
- We need the tokenizer binary/JSON and a small corpus (5-10 representative prompts) to run the tokenizer fidelity checks. If you can get Kevin to drop that in the intake doc link, I can kick off runs today.
- KV-cache layout mismatch: I can write a small adapter that normalizes the layout for the quantized path, but itll add ~6-8 hours of engineering time to validate. If we can accept the adapter as a temporary shim for the canary, we can get results fast.
- Telemetry: tag the canary with model_intake=zenith-orbit, intake_run=marcus-20260809. Also include variant_pin=true so cost shows separately in console.

I can own the compatibility run and will update by EOD tomorrow with pass/fail and a list of failing input buckets.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Lead ML Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zenith-Orbit model intake: urgent pin & compatibility scan

Marcus / Lauren —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answers: yes for a 48-hour canary pin on a small dedicated A100 pool; we can create an isolated routing rule that pins requests for the neuro-partner route to Zenith-Orbit v1.2 on the canary pool only. Impact to other customers will be zero if we keep the canary weight at <=2% of total traffic.

We need to do two things before turning the pin on:
1) infra checklist (attached pin-checklist.md) — ensures KV cache adapters are containerized and the rollout policy includes automatic rollback to v1.1 after 48h if error rates exceed 2% or latency regresses by 15%.
2) telemetry contract — please add the tags Lauren mentioned and ensure the eval emits the runtime metrics we use for automatic rollback (p99, error_rate, generation_token_edits).

If you anticipate keeping a pin for more than 72 hours well need Procurement/Legal approval (contract amendment for version-locking + usage SLO). Karthik: procurement trigger and notes: pin_period=48h; if extended, require MAP signature and 30-day notice on both sides.

Ive assigned a short canary slot for Aug 11 02:00-08:00 PST. Lauren, if you can feed the tokenizer artifacts and the 10 prompts by EOD Aug 10, infra will start the run.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pin-checklist.md (attachment stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Neil <kevin@neuroscale.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Zenith-Orbit model intake: urgent pin & compatibility scan

Kevin — looping you in with engineering. Plan below: 48-hour canary pin on a dedicated A100 pool (Aug 11 02:00-08:00 PST window), infra will tag telemetry and have automatic rollback triggers. Lauren is running tokenizer + KV compatibility checks and will report results. If we need >72 hours pinned, well ask for a signed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short amendment to the intake terms.

Ask for NeuroScale: please: 
- Share the tokenizer artifacts (binary + mapping) and the migration notes referenced in your manifest by EOD Aug 10 (attachment/drive link ok).
- Confirm youre ok with automatic fallback to v1.1 for the public partner route if we hit the rollback thresholds (2% error_rate or >15% latency regression).
- If there are IP/commercial constraints around pinning (weve seen requests to keep variant locks longer for partner demos), let us know up front so Legal can prepare the MAP.

Im attaching a draft MAP we use for short-term pins (MAP-NeuroScale-v1.docx). If NeuroScale can sign that ASAP it will avoid procurement delays should we need to extend the pin window.

Thanks everyone — will share canary run results and a short summary once Lauren posts the compatibility report.

Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Model Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-NeuroScale-v1.docx (attachment stub)
